Ulanow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ulanów, Poland

Not demolished. Ulanów's Jewish community, present from the town's founding in 1616, was home to a local Hasidic dynasty from the beginning of the 19th century; by 1939, Jews made up 56 percent of the town's population. This cemetery, likely established shortly after the town's founding, holds a first preserved tombstone dated 1681. During WWII, executions and unmarked mass burials took place there, and most tombstones were removed at the time and afterward. In the 1980s, the site was fenced with a brick gate, and recovered tombstones were placed within it; over 200 steles survive today, some richly decorated 19th-century examples.
